description: The value one site/data/series-<code>.js file assigns to window.__<prefix>SeriesReg['<num>'] (prefix is per-repo, e.g. __ffSeriesReg -- out of scope for a schema, which only covers the assigned object literal). `num` should match an entry in this repo's own index.js SERIES_ORDER (schema: index.schema.json) -- a cross-file constraint this single-file schema can't enforce itself.

num.description: Short code, e.g. 'I'..'XVI', 'MQ', 'SW', 'CC', 'DFF', 'DM', 'TR', 'EX', 'BE', 'WD', 'PB', 'FAN', 'Other', 'AN' -- per-repo, not a fixed enum.

url.description: Series-level wiki link. Omit or null for an unlinked heading.

note.description: Prose blurb under the heading. Same shape as a MediaDetails' `description`: a bare string (one paragraph), or an array of per-paragraph strings/TextSpan[] runs for inline <em>/<abbr> styling.

chronoOrder.description: Series sort key for Chronological mode. Defaults to 0 when omitted.

recommendedOrder.description: Series sort key for Narrative mode (the default). Defaults to 0 when omitted.

media.description: One entry per checkbox-row slot. Renamed from `games` -- this series' items are routinely Books/Comics/Movies/etc, not just Games (see MediaType).

DateValue.description: titleDate / subtitleDate. A plain year, a full date optionally carrying a two-digit same-day tie-break ord suffix (' 10' / ' 20'), or a {start,end} range for the handful of multi-year pseudo-entries (`end` may be an open-ended '<year>+').

TextSpan.description: One inline styled run of text (rendered by TextSpan.dc.html as a single <span>: plain/em/abbr/tooltip/linked-em/JP-tag). Used inside a Prose paragraph (description/note). A bare string auto-wraps to {text}.

tip.description: Tooltip text. Required alongside tipText/hintText; optional alongside text/emText (e.g. { emText: ' (EU)', tip: 'Europe', helpStyle: 'cursor: help;' }).

jpTag.description: Appends ' (JP)'. Unrelated to a PlatformItem's own jpTag field.

helpStyle.description: Extra inline CSS on the wrapping span, e.g. 'cursor: help;'.

Prose.description: Shared shape for `description` (MediaDetails/VersionDetails) and the series-level `note`: a bare string (one plain paragraph), or an array where each item is a plain string (one paragraph) or a nested TextSpan[] run (one paragraph built from styled parts).

BylinePart.description: bylineParts[] item -- EntryByline.dc.html's own narrower shape, not the same object as TextSpan.

label.description: Prefixes this segment AND implies a line break before it -- a labeled segment always starts its own line (e.g. an FFXI expansion name, or 'Comrades ' before a spin-off mode's own length). Write it as the first key when present, as a visual cue. Redundant (harmless) to also set `br` on the previous segment; the renderer emits at most one line break for the shared boundary either way.

tip.description: Tooltip, e.g. 'Main Story' / 'Main + Extra' / 'Completionist', or a custom tip like 'Solo' / 'Co-op' / 'Vs.'.

join.description: Overrides the joiner rendered after this segment (default ' / ' between any two consecutive segments, nothing after the last). Rare -- e.g. ', ' before an unrelated segment tacked onto the same line.

br.description: Line break after this segment, no joiner text. See `label` -- setting both on adjoining segments for the same boundary is redundant but harmless.

Length.description: A bare string (unstructured, e.g. '224p; P'), or an array of LengthPart segments (e.g. Main Story / Main + Extra / Completionist, joined by ' / ' unless overridden).

value.description: A code from catalogs.js's LANGUAGE_NAMES, or the literal '…?' sentinel. Displayed verbatim as the badge text (with LANGUAGE_NAMES[value] as its tooltip) -- not a pure catalog lookup key like PlatformItem.key, so it keeps its own name rather than being renamed to `key`.

native.description: Marks the original/source language. Not read by any component -- annotation only, kept for real data compatibility.

voice.description: Full audio/voiced. Mutually exclusive with textOnly in practice.

tip.description: Explicit tooltip override, used verbatim with no auto ' — full audio'/' — text only' suffix.

key.description: Looked up in platform-icons.js's PLATFORM_ICONS to merge in iconImg/iconSize/imgStyle/jpTag/base name.

url.description: This release's own link. Unset falls back to the enclosing VersionDetails/MediaDetails' own `platformsUrl` if it has one.

name.description: Full override of the displayed label, bypassing the catalog base-label + paren composition -- only legitimate on a key platform-icons.js flags `nameOverride: true` for (a categorically different medium word `paren` can't produce, e.g. `book`'s 'Manga'/'Short Stories', since `paren` only ever appends). scripts/validate-data.py fails a `name` on any other key -- use `paren` instead.

paren.description: Appends " (<paren>)" to the catalog's base label. Mutually exclusive with `name` in practice (name wins if both given).

jpTag.description: Shows the visible '(jp)' marker AND auto-appends ' (Japan Only)' to the composed tooltip -- don't also hand-type '(Japan Only)' into `name`/`paren`.

nonJpTag.description: Shows the visible '(non-jp)' marker AND auto-appends ' (Non-Japan Only)' to the composed tooltip -- don't also hand-type it into `name`/`paren`.

terminated.description: Dims + strikes through the icon AND auto-appends '; terminated' to the composed tooltip -- don't also hand-type 'terminated' into `name`/`paren`.

noResults.description: Dims the icon (same as `terminated`, no strike) AND auto-appends '; no results yet' to the composed tooltip -- don't also hand-type it, and there is no separate opacity override (every real use was the same dim level).

noUrl.description: Common in real data alongside a null/absent url, but not read by any current template -- authoring annotation only.

prefix.description: Short text prefix before the icon (unlinked-icon render path), e.g. 'U' for an UltraHD Blu-ray variant.

icon.description: Bootstrap Icons class, alternative to iconImg.

text.description: Plain text badge instead of an icon.

search.description: Computes `url` as a search instead of stating the encoded URL by hand. Requires `term`.

term.description: The search query text (near-required alongside `search` -- default results are poor with none).

searchSuffix.description: Overrides the per-key default suffix word(s) appended after `term` (platform-icons.js's own `searchSuffix`, e.g. fan-movie -> 'game movie'). '' suppresses it entirely.

key.description: Looked up in catalogs.js's RATING_KINDS. Score-mode entries supply `label` (a tooltip, e.g. 'Metacritic'); badge-mode entries (`textOnly: true` in the catalog, e.g. 'nyr'/'tbd'/'favorable'/'unfavorable') supply `abbrTerm`/`abbrDef` or a bare `score` -- either way an entry states only `key`, never repeats the catalog's own text. Special-cased 'steam' (score is a STEAM_REVIEW_LABELS abbreviation).

score.description: Required unless `key`'s catalog entry already supplies one (a textOnly badge kind).

label.description: Explicit tooltip override for score-mode, or explicit badge text for badge-mode -- the escape hatch for a rating source with no RATING_KINDS entry at all.

textOnly.description: Plain text/abbr badge, not a link. Implied automatically when `key`'s catalog entry has textOnly:true -- set directly only for a genuine one-off with no catalog key (rare after `favorable`/`unfavorable` were added; prefer a catalog key over this).

MediaSlot.description: One item in `media[]` -- one checkbox-row slot. `releases[0]` is the primary row; `releases[1:]` are inline "or <title>" rows on the same line, in display order. Each release is fully self-contained (own mediaType/chronoOrder/recommendedOrder/etc, not shared across the slot) so promoting/reordering/moving a release is a pure array operation, never a field-by-field reshape.

VersionDetails.description: The full content shape for one release or one of its collapsible versions[] items -- title through listItems. A node with no own title/subtitle inherits title/titleUrl/titleDate/titleItalic wholesale from its immediate parent (all-or-nothing) -- not enforceable in this single-node schema. Recursion is bounded: a VersionDetails has no `versions` of its own (only MediaDetails does, one level), so a versions[] item can't nest further versions.

titleItalic.description: Italicizes the title -- for a non-game media work, since game titles render plain/bold by default.

id.description: Manual override of the derived slug/anchor id. Currently unused in real data but a valid escape hatch.

label.description: Deprecated/legacy freeform display text, paired with `url`. Still rendered ahead of the title/subtitle output when present -- prefer title/subtitle for new entries.

url.description: Deprecated/legacy link paired with `label`. Distinct from platformsUrl/profileUrl.

chronoOrder.description: Sort key for Chronological mode, read off `releases[0]` (`releases[0].chronoOrder ?? 0`). Kept on every release/version (not hoisted to a shared MediaSlot field) so promoting one to be the new `releases[0]` never requires a second edit elsewhere. Distinct from the series-level chronoOrder.

recommendedOrder.description: Sort key for Narrative mode (the default), read off `releases[0]` (`releases[0].recommendedOrder ?? 0`). Same self-containment rationale as chronoOrder. Distinct from the series-level recommendedOrder.

mainline.description: Counted for the intro's mainlineCount stat, read off `releases[0]`.

tags.description: Free-text byline words (joined with ' · ' unless bylineParts is set). 'Expansion' and 'DLC' reclassify a Game for stats-counting; 'Optional' excludes a release from the release-order pseudo-series' earliest-date computation. Everything else is display text only -- do not enum-restrict.

bylineParts.description: Alternative to a tags-derived byline, for an inline <abbr> in the byline. Wins over tags for display; tags are still read for their 'Expansion'/'DLC'/'Optional' semantics even when this is set.

ratings.description: One item per independently-resolved score/badge source -- no fixed critic/user slots, no separate score-link-vs-badge object shapes. Renamed from the singular `rating`.

platforms.description: Flat -- no grouping. (Grouping used to control flex-wrap positions, but every render path already flattens it via `.flat()` before display and re-sorts by catalog order regardless of source order, so it had zero effect on the rendered output; dropped rather than kept as unused structure.)

platformsUrl.description: Fallback URL for any `platforms` item lacking its own url, on this same release/version.

profileUrl.description: "Profile ↗" link next to the Platforms label header. Renamed from `storeUrl` to match its own rendered label.

langOrder.description: Per-entry override of the default language sort-priority order (default ['JA','EN']).

listTitle.description: FFXI-style linked heading rendered as a plain <ul> under the description, alongside listItems.

listItems.description: Plain strings only, no parts support.

MediaDetails.description: A `releases[]` item: the same content shape as VersionDetails (title through listItems -- kept as a literal duplicate of VersionDetails' own `properties` here, not an `allOf`/$ref composition, because scripts/validate-data.py's hand-rolled validator doesn't implement `unevaluatedProperties` and an `allOf` branch's own `additionalProperties: false` would wrongly reject this def's extra `versions` field; AJV alone would've been fine with the composed form), plus its own collapsible `versions[]` ("other versions and platforms" toggle list). Each release has an independent versions[] -- not shared across the enclosing MediaSlot. Keep this in sync with VersionDetails by hand if either changes.
